About the School
At Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge we are committed to helping our students realise their dreams by equipping our young people with the knowledge, skills, understanding and confidence to achieve success.
Expectations of ourselves, our students and the wider community of the school are high. We provide a rich and varied curriculum as well as an extensive range of extra-curricular and sporting activities.
Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge students are confident, talented, inspirational and have a hunger to learn. The greater the challenge, the more they achieve.
Being part of the Maiden Erlegh Trust means everyone benefits from a wealth of experience in inspiring young people to achieve their full potential. Staff are dedicated and hard working professionals.
This website will give you a flavour of Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge and will allow you to find out more about our values.

NEWS & CALENDAR
NEWS & CALENDAR
Latest News
SEND Parent and Carer Forum – Register to take part
Parents and carers are invited to register interest in a new SEND Parent and Carer Forum, bringing together parents and carers from across all schools in Maiden Erlegh Trust.
The forum will provide an opportunity for families of pupils with additional needs to help inform SEND priorities, shape future provision, and contribute to the development of the next SEND strategy. This work will be co-produced with families from the outset.
The forum will be led by Kelly Nash, School Improvement Director: SEND, and Neil Strain, Director of Special Education Hub, who work across our schools to strengthen SEND provision and inclusive practice.
The forum will meet three times a year and is likely to be held online to support accessibility. It will focus on SEND priorities and provision across schools.
Parents and carers of pupils with additional needs who would like to take part are invited to register via the online form or QR code shared by their school. Further details will be shared with those who register.
Scan the QR code below to get involved!
Please note: the forum will focus on SEND priorities and provision across schools and is not a forum for discussing individual pupils or cases.

Latest News
New PE clubs this term
We want to share details of some new PE clubs that are getting started this term.
Being involved in something active, outside and as part of a team has so many benefits – please do encourage your sons & daughters to explore the full range of what is on offer.
Cross-country club is on Thursdays; a great way to boost your mind and mood, access to the Fitness Suite is now on Wednesday and Thursday, and Rounders club is after-school on Tuesdays.
We are also really pleased to have renewed our link with Henley Rowing Club, with two groups of students heading out onto the Thames each week to develop their rowing skills.

CAREERS, WORK EXPERIENCE & WORK RELATED LEARNING
CAREERS, WORK EXPERIENCE & WORK RELATED LEARNING
Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) at Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge is seen as an important part of school life and all students will receive this as part of their learning here at the school. We are committed to providing the appropriate activities and experiences to enable students to make successful transitions from Foundation Stage to Key Stage 4 and further education, training programmes, apprenticeships or work.
Our school's careers programme embed equality and diversity considerations throughout.
Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edges' aims in relation to CEIAG are:
Careers education at Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge should not just be seen as learning about jobs but also learning about work ethics, equipping students with skills (both hard and soft) for the work place, ensuring transition occurs smoothly and helping to reduce barriers to entering the world of work.
In this section you will find lots of useful links and information about careers, services, further education and training programmes including: information on careers fairs, volunteering, work experience etc.
For more information on CEIAG and how it is delivered please click on the position paper and mapping page on the left hand side.
All students in Year 10 are supported in securing a Work Experience place (to be completed in early May). We proudly work with OXLEP to help students source placements and ensure that all relevant Health and Safety Checks are complete. Students also undertake a series of workshops to ensure they are ‘workplace-ready’ ahead of completing their placement.
All students at Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge will have a careers interview in Year 11. If you would like to have a careers appointment please speak to your tutor or Mrs J Hills (j.hills@maidenerleghtrust.org)
All students will also undertake a mock interview to help them prepare for College/Sixth Form progression and beyond. The interviews will be conducted by senior members of staff from other Trust schools, Trust Central Services and Trustees and local business men and women.
Individual guidance is supported by a wide selection of reference material and software in the school’s careers library. In Year 11 to support with career choices, workshops and seminars are held in the spring term; where employees from various careers give talks to the students. Within the PHSE programme in Years 7-11, supported by the tutor and assembly programmes there are a series of sessions based around careers and work related learning.
Please find attached below the Provider Access Policy for Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge.
If you wish to discuss the careers programme further, please contact our school Lead for Careers and Destinations Mrs J Hills (j.hills@maidenerleghtrust.org).

pageCache.pageTitle: Science fair - Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge
pageCache.text:
NEWS & CALENDAR
NEWS & CALENDAR
Latest News
Science fair
On Friday we hosted the Science Fair. There were well over 50 student stands from Year 7-10 which varied from posters about particular scientists, specific discoveries to personal areas of interest and research.
Students then presented their research to other students and staff. It was lovely to hear their enthusiasm and confidence in their presentations – the content of which was hugely varied – the prevalence of ACL injuries in female athletes, the science of DeJaVu, marine bioluminescence, the life cycle of a star, the work of Rutherford and Edison and the process of nuclear fusion! A huge thank you to Mr Mav and the Science team for their encouragement of all students to take part and to the students themselves for embracing the challenge!

PARENTS
REMOTE LEARNING PROVISION
REMOTE LEARNING PROVISION
Here you can find the school’s plans for remote provision in the event of unexpected school closure.
Teaching & Learning Contingency Plan
When the school is closed or partially closed due to industrial action the school will do its best to offer remote learning however this provision may be limited due to staff not being available to set work.
If you are experiencing issues with technology (including accessing Google Classroom) please contact your son/daughter’s tutor in the first instance
If your son/daughter is unwell and will not be attending lessons on a given day please email: meceabsenceandmedical@maidenerleghtrust.org
All other concerns regarding Remote Provision should be directed to Emma Bliss, Headteacher by emailing: e.bliss@maidenerleghtrust.org

pageCache.pageTitle: SEE WHAT PARENTS SAY ABOUT US ... - Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge
pageCache.text:
ABOUT US
SEE WHAT PARENTS SAY ABOUT US ...
SEE WHAT PARENTS SAY ABOUT US ...
"Our daughter has been at MECE for the last 2 years. We also have an older child at another local secondary school and have been able to see both schools in action. All schools have their issues but we have been constantly impressed by how caring and supportive the staff and leadership are at MECE around our daughters individual needs. We often have phone calls home to explain and expand on things within the day - both positive events and when concerns need to be raised. When we have raised issues they have been dealt with effectively and efficiently. We are constantly amazed at the breadth and range of sporting opportunities that are on offer and the way all children are encouraged far beyond the academic curriculum. The staffing issues from last year appear to behind them and we couldn’t be more delighted with the new head and her experience and focus."
Year 8 Parent, 2024-25
"We have been so happy with MECE since our daughter started there a year and a half ago. She has grown hugely in confidence and has been offered so many wonderful opportunities to be involved in extra-curricular activities - particularly sports. She has been asked to join tournaments for football, rugby, netball and hockey and now also does a weekly rowing club which offers potential opportunities to do a course at Henley Rowing club next Summer. There was also a wonderful opportunity for her to star in the recent ‘Bugsy Malone’ play! She attends a different club every lunchtime including ‘Christian lunch club’ which was started after our daughter, asked the R.S teacher if there was a Christian Union at MECE and the teacher offered to start one! The School have been so supportive and accommodating about our views as Christians and this has been so refreshing. At the recent parents evening, we were able to meet a variety of teaching staff and they all came across as passionate about their subjects and like they really knew our daughter, which made a big impression. We love the ‘small school approach’ and nurturing environment MECE provides and we are so glad we chose for our daughter to come to secondary school here!"
Year 8 Parent, 2024-25
"Our experience at MECE particularly with the SEN staff and teachers has been great, not just for our child but also us as parents. After a difficult primary school experience, we are grateful for the collaborative and transparent approach at MECE which is a breath of fresh air. Our child is listened to, involved in decisions and treated with dignity and understanding. It's been a long journey, with plenty of bumps along the way, but we are seeing the positive results of a dedicated and compassionate approach. We feel we are all part of the same team working together to help our child reach their full potential. Additionally, all the staff at school are so nice, from reception, office staff, TAs and teachers - I see them treat all the children as individuals and they seem to know everyone by first name. This creates a warm, welcoming environment and strong sense of community."
Year 9 Parent, 2024-25
"Our children joined MECE in 2024 and have transitioned into secondary school very happily. This smooth transition was in no small part due to the wonderful, caring staff. In particular, Mr Groves went out of his way to ensure new friendships were established during those early days and that his tutor group were all feeling comfortable and at ease in their new surroundings. Mr Groves is always available to support the children in his role as a Year 7 Tutor, and is very happy to liaise with parents when extra guidance or support is needed. Outstanding - an absolute credit to the MECE family in every way! MECE offers an impressive array of extra-curricular clubs, which are available every lunchtime and after school. My son and daughter really enjoy playing a wide range of sports with their friends at lunchtime, including volleyball, basketball, fitness in the gym, table tennis and badminton. There is always something to do, and I am grateful that MECE offers brilliant activities for the students to get involved in together. There is plenty of choice, and you are free to dip in and out when you feel like having a go. Additionally, my son has been really excited to be able to join the rowing club on a Friday after school, and is looking forward to the opportunity to get onto the water in the summer. Since joining MECE in Sept 2024, there have been a number of varied and interesting (optional) competitions set across the curriculum for the students to participate in and enjoy, including science, art, story writing and photography, to name a few. One of the many advantages of being part of a smaller community is the feeling of being 'seen' and noticed and there really is something for everyone. MECE has a striking and smart uniform which is worn with pride, and was actually one of the many reasons my children really liked the school. It is a point of difference between other local schools, and very much to be encouraged."
Year 7 Parent, 2024-25
"I love how responsive MECE is to enquiries I may have in regards my daughter’s progress and well-being. The HOY ‘s in every year have been amazing. I really feel like MECE knows me and my child. Sport The PE dept at MECE are outstanding. They have introduced so many new sports to the school and offer clubs at lunch and after school. They really encourage all children to take part and find something they enjoy and progress in. Leadership Miss Bliss has stepped in to the role of Head like she has done it forever. The children seem to have had a seamless transition from Mrs Bowers to Miss Bliss and seem very happy she has stepped up. Miss Bliss clearly loves the school and that shines from her. Extracurricular My daughter’s year have had some amazing opportunities! Belgium, France, skiing, Iceland, DoE. You would never think a small school could do so much!"
Year 9 Parent, 2024-25
"My daughter is currently in Year 8. We chose MECE when she was in year 6 as we were impressed by the targeted learning groups, the variety of extra-curricular activities on offer, the school being a close-knit community and the connected approach to learning through lots of diverse educational opportunities.
Our daughter is thriving at MECE - she is challenged in lessons, has gone on lots of school trips, joined many academic and sports clubs, participated in sporting fixtures and feels very settled. The teachers know her and have a great understanding of her learning and her as a person. There have been changes in leadership, but core staff, who are experienced and engaging, have stayed, so the change in headteacher hasn’t impacted our daughter. It has been a very positive start to her secondary education."
Year 8 Parent, 2024-25
"My son is thriving at MECE. At the recent Y8 parents evening, talking to his teachers, I could tell that they all know him well and are keen to praise him for his achievements and encourage him to work on areas to improve. I feel they know how to get the best from him in his learning. I've been particularly happy with the sport options, a wide range of activities in PE lessons and after-school clubs and fixtures against other schools. He is also part of a lovely friendship group, all new friends since starting at MECE. I highly recommend the school."
Year 8 Parent, 2024-25
"We have been more than happy with the quality of teaching that MECE has given our daughter. We feel that her teachers know her well and given her support when needed. As parents, it has been wonderful to see her progress so well across all subjects. We really like that her achievements are acknowledged both with her and with us receiving teachers' comments. We are incredibly glad our daughter chose to attend MECE over another local secondary school and would highly recommend that any potential families give it serious consideration as an option."
Year 10 Parent, 2024-25
"The sports department at MECE is second to none. Mr Caldwell has brought in so many different sports for the students to try and enjoy, rowing archery and many more. I can’t recommend Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge enough. All three of my children have been through the school."
Year 9 Parent, 2024-25
"I’m very impressed by the high expectations for behaviour, learning, effort and achievement. The pupils are well-behaved and academically gifted, ready to learn and have created strong friendships."
Year 8 Parent, 2024-25
"Can I just mention how important it is that my child gets the support that they do in school - despite outward appearances they struggle hugely at times and support from CAMHS is proving pretty difficult to come by.
The level of care given as well as general provision has been fantastic, particularly from Mr Harte, Miss Brown and Miss Cheeseman."
"Please could you pass on our thanks to the members of staff who were involved with organising/leading the trip to Merl and Reading Uni. It is so lovely when the students can take their learning out of school and see new things and new places. Even just negotiating the buses in order to get to somewhere unfamiliar was a good experience.
Many thanks. We really appreciate the extra effort given in order to make sure things like this happen."
Year 8 Parent, 2023-24
"To all the members of staff who were involved in making the practice expedition happen this weekend.
My husband didn't get a chance to say thank you to anyone at pick up today so can I just say a huge thank you to everyone involved. Taking precious time out of your weekend to spend with a group of teenagers is definitely above and beyond. My son was in years 5 and 6 during the Covid lockdowns which meant he (and his classmates) missed out on residentials, big days out etc. This is the first time he has been 'away overnight' with school ever. He had a great time but more than that, we have noticed a real difference in him socially during the past months. The year 9 children in his Duke of Edinburgh group are actually talking to each other out of school. They even went on a long practice walk to 'break in walking shoes' a couple of weeks ago which absolutely would not have happened in a million years before being part of this award scheme.
I know it's not over yet, but thank you. These sorts of experiences mean so much and are totally reliant on the kindness and generosity of people like yourselves. We really appreciate it. You are all amazing."
Year 9 Parent, 2023-24
"To Mrs Chopra and all the staff who supported the Duke of Edinburgh weekend.
Thank you for giving up your time and energy to give the students this experience. My son had a great time and it has been especially positive for him in terms of building relationships with his peers.
Have a good last week of term and enjoy a well earned break."
Year 9 Parent, 2023-24
"My child is definitely enjoying History and it’s good to hear his efforts and focus have been noticed. Funnily enough he was talking about his Cold War lessons earlier this week, educating me on the causes and consequences, and how interesting it all was. You’re obviously doing a super job so a big thank you to you."
Year 9 Parent, 2023-24
"Please can you pass on our thanks to Ms Biddiss - she clearly is a dedicated & wonderful teacher and is making a positive difference to these students' lives!!"
Year 11 Parent, 2023-24
" Finally, I would like to just pass on a huge thank you to you all of the staff who have been supporting (my child). Despite all of his issues, he is happy to come to school every day and that is down to an amazing team of supportive and inclusive staff. You are all amazing and I hope you all know how very much appreciated you are."
Year 7 Parent, 2023-24
"Another brilliantly well organised parent’s evening – thank you all! Possibly the most important one with the mock exam results being issued. Teachers were really well-prepared and provided really useful comments, feedback and guidance that (as always!) left us feeling they really knew the students. It was also really useful to have the handouts with the key information for each subject.
We were also pleased to see Mrs Bowers in attendance and taking the opportunity not only to talk to parents, but also to the students about their results. Thank you to everyone."
Year 11 Parent, 2023-24
"I would like to nominate Miss Cheeseman and the staff working in the hive. They have helped my child through a difficult week and kept me informed and made her feel supported. This is invaluable in her feeling ready to attend lessons and learn to the best of her ability at school. Thankyou to you all, we as parents really appreciate it."
Year 7 Parent, 2023-24
"I want to thank Mr Mount for his assembly last week. My Year 11 is a bit jaded when it comes to assemblies, especially those focussed on annual events where she feels she’s heard it all before! However, she was full of interest and enthusiasm for Mr Mount’s assembly and said it was fascinating as it was so personal to him. She said she wished she’d taken history as an option, and you can’t get much more positive praise than that! Thank you!
Year 11 Parent, 2023-24
"I just wanted to say how grateful I am to Mrs Hussain for her support during the mocks. Her support last week was really completely over and above what was necessary and was a huge help.
I would be very grateful if you could do something to recognise this amazing support, as I say, completely beyond what was required but of immense benefit."
Year 11 Parent, 2023-24

PARENTS
WRAPAROUND & HOLIDAY CHILDCARE
WRAPAROUND & HOLIDAY CHILDCARE
Wraparound childcare are activities and supervision which take place before school childcare and after school childcare (up to 6pm or later).
Holiday childcare is childcare that is available through schools during the school holidays.
Parents have a right to request wraparound provision up to the end of Year 9 from the school that their child attends.
If you wish to request wraparound provision you should write to the Head of the school in question.
In that letter you must:
At the end of each term we will collate any requests that have come in. Where we receive requests from 4% or more of Years 7 to 9 in any one year, we will review the requests.
The requests will be evaluated in light of:
We would aim to make a decision within two weeks of the start of the Spring term and two weeks at the start of the Summer term.
Where we do not feel we can provide some or all of the requests, we will inform parents with reasons.
Where we feel we can move to providing some or all of the requests, we will inform parents of provisional costs and consult more widely to ensure there is firm demand.
We will then confirm the time scales in which we would aim to establish the care (given recruitment time scales etc) and the final costs.
We would aim to run a pilot of one term in the first instance and if demand is confirmed we would establish regular provision which would be reviewed on a six monthly basis.

The true highlight of last week was our whole-school production of Sister Act Jnr. The performances were simply fantastic and a wonderful showcase of the talent within our school community. On Thursday we celebrated our Year 11 students completing five years with us. There was a wonderful blend of excitement and poignancy as we gathered for their final assembly. CURRICULUM
Personal Development
Personal Development
At Maiden Erlegh Chiltern Edge we recognise the personal development of students is a fundamental part of our academic and pastoral work. It is our intention to create good local, national and global citizens, who develop good character and resilience. To this end, we aim to develop students spiritually, morally, socially and culturally and ensure that they are treated as individuals whilst doing this. We aim to teach students about British values, mutual respect and tolerance.
We aim to deliver spiritual, moral, social and cultural education through all aspects of school life; curriculum, extra-curricular activities, the pastoral system, assemblies as well as themed events.
Our Personal Development provision follows the recommendations laid out by the Department for Education and the PSHE Association.
The PSHE Association suggest that Personal Development education should be treated and timetabled in the same way as any other subject, with one hour long, discrete lesson a week.
The 2019 statutory Health Education, Relationships Education and RSE guidance also states that: Schools should have the same high expectations of the quality of pupils’ work in these subjects as for other curriculum areas. A strong curriculum will build on the knowledge pupils have previously acquired, including in other subjects, with regular feedback provided on pupil progress. This would be very difficult to achieve without dedicated, discrete PSHE lessons.
Topics for all students are grouped into 7 core themes:
These sessions will be relevant to the age, understanding, cultural background and circumstances of the students. They will also reflect their needs in terms of language, learning styles and abilities.
Emotional Wellbeing
Citizen and Community
Careers, Work Experience and Work Related Learning

Risk and Safety

Astronomy Evening
Last week we held our Annual Astronomy Evening in conjunction with the Reading Astronomical Society
Sadly, for the first time in many years, the weather did not play ball and even the impressive telescopes that members of RAS brought along weren’t able to see through the low cloud cover and drizzle. However, those that came were not left disappointed with RAS members sharing stunning photography and facts about space and students (and parents) were able to still test out some of the telescopes. Fingers crossed for next year.
